To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the upstream region of the GST Ya contains at least four nuclear protein-binding sequences.

the upstream region of the GST Ya enhancer contains four protein-binding sites that include two sites bound by constitutive hepatocyte factors and one site bound by a protein induced by 3-methyl cholantherene (3-MC), which is required for inducibility of the Ya gene.
The GST Ya gene is expressed in all hepatocytes but can be induced 20-fold in the pericentral cells of the liver.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of the GST Ya promoter and the proteins involved in this regulation.
the regulation of a gene whose product, GST Ya, is involved in the metabolism of a variety of toxic chemicals.
the identification of the upstream elements and the nature of proteins that regulate the expression of the xenobiotics inducible GST Ya gene in hepatocytes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the upstream sequences of the rat GST Ya gene are complex.
the GST Ya gene is expressed in hepatocytes, and the upstream region of the gene contains sequences required and sufficient for cell specificity and inducible regulation.
this GST Ya gene has a complex enhancer that contains several nuclear protein-binding sites, including one for an inducible protein, two for HNF1 and one for HNF4.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the upstream region from -980 to the transcription initiation site of the GST Ya is required and sufficient to confer both constitutive and induced expression of this gene.
the 5' flanking region of the GST Ya is composed of a complex of cis-acting elements that are responsible for the cell-specific and inducer-specific expression of this gene.

the GST Ya gene has a constitutive enhancer region that contains two binding sites for constitutive liver-specific nuclear factors, and an inducible region that contains one or more binding sites for proteins induced by 3MC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the upstream region of the GST Ya promoter has the potential for multiple levels of regulation.
a single enhancer can be regulated by a combination of constitutive and inducible transcription factors.
the expression of GST Ya is regulated by multiple factors that bind to multiple sites within the enhancer region of the GST Ya promoter.
